citation: Moura, N., Vidal, M., Aguilera, A. M., Vilas-Boas, J. P., Serra, S. & Leman, M. (2023). Knee flexion of saxophone players anticipates tonal context of music. npj Science of Learning 8:22. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-023-00172-z
title: R-package for computational modeling of the auditory periphery (ANI, pitch expectation, rhythmical density)
description: The authors released "the routines for the computational modeling of the auditory periphery ... freely available as an R-package at a Github repository". It computes the auditory nerve image with CalcANI, periodicity pitch images with PeriodicityPitch, pitch expectation profiles with ContextualityIndex (Comparison), and rhythmical density with RoughnessFFT. The package implements the model used to derive pitch expectation and rhythmical density profiles from audio in this study.
requirements: Mono audio recordings of the performance, converted into a 40-channel auditory nerve image.
target_learning_goals: analyzing sensorimotor coupling in performance data

article_title: The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education.
citation: Almasi-Turk Sahar, Roozbehi Amrollah. (2026). The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09833-0
title: R-ISAM: a five-phase spiral framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education
description: R-ISAM is a five-phase spiral curriculum model integrating gross anatomy, histology, and embryology with radiology, surface anatomy, physical examination, and clinical reasoning. As the article states, "R-ISAM consists of five sequential phases that progressively integrate anatomical sciences with clinical reasoning, imaging interpretation, and procedural skills". The phases run from System Overview through Anatomical Radiology, Surface Anatomy, and System Examination to Integrated Clinical Anatomy, each building on the previous one. It is grounded in the spiral curriculum, Cognitive Load Theory, the ICAP framework, and alignment with CBME and Entrustable Professional Activities.
requirements: Sustained collaboration between basic science and clinical faculty, including joint planning meetings, workshops, and peer observation
Robust infrastructure: digital repositories, simulation facilities, small-group learning spaces, and online platforms for integrated content and assessments
Student support mechanisms including peer mentoring, formative feedback, and targeted academic assistance
constraints: Phases I and V are fixed, whereas Phases II, III, and IV can be rearranged or merged, expanded into four phases, or condensed into two
Phases I through IV can be planned and delivered within 8 to 10 weeks of a standard 16-week semester
target_learners: Undergraduate medical students in Basic Sciences through Clerkship stages
target_learning_goals: Clinical reasoning and physical examination skills
examples: Implemented across musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal systems between 2020 and 2025 in an undergraduate medical program, with more than 700 students exposed
key_sources: Almasi-Turk Sahar, Roozbehi Amrollah. (2026). The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09833-0

article_title: The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education.
citation: Almasi-Turk Sahar, Roozbehi Amrollah. (2026). The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09833-0
title: 65-item R-ISAM evaluation questionnaire with seven domains
description: A 65-item questionnaire developed to evaluate R-ISAM across seven domains (Basic Sciences Integration, Spiral Progression, Clinical Integration, Educational Environment, Teaching Methods, Assessment & Feedback, Overall Satisfaction). It was developed through item generation with an expert panel (n = 5 anatomy educators), content validity assessment using the Content Validity Index, pilot testing with 25 students, and reliability analysis. "The final instrument demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.989)" and factor analysis confirmed a seven-domain structure explaining 71.4% of variance.
requirements: Content validity assessment using the Content Validity Index and pilot testing before deployment
constraints: Developed and validated at a single institution with an anatomy-education focus
target_learners: Undergraduate medical students across Basic Sciences, Physiopathology, and Clerkship stages
target_learning_goals: Evaluation of perceived integration, teaching quality, assessment, and satisfaction in an integrated anatomy curriculum
examples: Administered simultaneously to all three stage groups during a single week with no examinations scheduled; response rate 27.5% (206 of 750 eligible students)
